### 2) What each goal means (and is not intended to mean) in this application

- **g0 Reduce fatigue throughout the day**: Use the platform to feel less mentally tired (e.g., micro-breaks, pleasant distraction). *Not* a medical treatment claim.
- **g1 Provide entertainment during periods of boredom**: Offer content/features that fill idle moments. *Not* guaranteeing constant novelty.
- **g2 Enable relaxation and winding down between activities**: Support decompression (calm viewing/listening). *Not* necessarily sleep.
- **g3 Play video content**: Core capability to play videos. *Not* limited to a specific format.
- **g4 Select a video to play**: Choose any item from feed/search/history. *Not* implying creation/upload.
- **g5 Continue video playback while browsing other content**: Keep playing while exploring within the app. *Not* necessarily leaving the app.
- **g6 Access and watch recommended short-form videos**: Enter a shorts feed driven by recommendations. *Not* searching.
- **g7 Select and play a specific short-form video**: Pick a particular short (from results/history). *Not* autoplay-only.
- **g8 Search for long-form content to watch**: Use search for longer videos. *Not* browsing-only discovery.
- **g9 Play long-form content in the background while doing other tasks**: Background long-form playback while multitasking. *Not* requiring video on screen.
- **g10 Estimate weekly time spent creating long-form videos**: A creator-analytics type metric. *Not* viewing time; implies creator mode/insights.
- **g11 View long-form content recommendations**: Recommendations specifically for long videos. *Not* shorts.
- **g12 Filter search results to show long-form content longer than 20 minutes**: Duration filter threshold use-case. *Not* the only duration filter.
- **g13 Provide a personalized content feed based on viewing history and watching habits**: Personalization using implicit behavior signals. *Not* only explicit interests.
- **g14 Enable consuming content through audio without needing to watch visual cues**: Audio-first consumption (background, screen-off, PiP). *Not* transcripts/subtitles.
- **g15 Allow users to scroll to browse more content until they find something they like**: Infinite scrolling/browsing. *Not* structured navigation only.
- **g16 Allow users to easily understand and navigate available options while watching a video**: Clear player UI, controls, menus. *Not* a redesign mandate.
- **g17 Automatically play another short video after the current video finishes**: Shorts autoplay sequence. *Not* user must select each time.
- **g18 Allow video playback to continue in the background while the user switches tasks or tabs**: Background across tabs/apps. *Not* limited to long-form.
- **g19 Pause video playback on demand**: Basic control. *Not* advanced bookmarking.
- **g20 Allow users to scroll to find and resume a previously unfinished video**: Resume partially watched items (likely long-form). *Not* necessarily cross-device sync.
- **g21 Allow users to find a previously watched short video again**: Re-find a short via history/search. *Not* guaranteed if history disabled.
- **g22 Temporarily stop recommending certain types of videos and later resume showing new content**: Snooze/block topic categories. *Not* permanent deletion.
- **g23 Select content to watch based on current mood**: Mood-driven discovery (filters, prompts). *Not* clinical mood detection.
- **g24 Engage in multiple activities simultaneously**: User multitasking goal (why). *Not* app running multiple videos at once.
- **g25 Quickly occupy attention to provide distraction**: Fast-start content to distract briefly. *Not* addiction/compulsion as a requirement.
- **g26 Play background content to keep part of attention engaged while completing other tasks and maintaining focus**: “Companion media” while working. *Not* productivity tool per se.
- **g27 Explore a subject in greater depth**: Use long-form/technical content to learn deeply. *Not* formal certification.
- **g28 Spend time alone to mentally disengage**: Solitary decompression aided by media. *Not* social features.

- **g30 Adjust audio playback volume, including muting**: Volume/mute controls. *Not* equalizer.
- **g31 Use time to unwind**: General relaxation intent. *Not* necessarily sleep.
- **g32 Keep an activity history enabled while minimizing visible negatives**: Keep history for usefulness while hiding embarrassing/undesired signals. *Not* deleting everything.
- **g33 Revisit previously viewed content**: Go back to watched items. *Not* necessarily offline downloads.
- **g34 Temporarily hide or reset viewing history without permanently deleting it**: “Pause history” or temporary reset. *Not* irreversible deletion.
- **g35 Play media in the background**: General background playback capability. *Not* only video; could be audio.
- **g36 Search for short videos using remembered details**: Query by partial memory. *Not* browsing feed.
- **g37 Retrieve previously watched short videos**: Pull from history/library. *Not* share necessarily.
- **g38 Share previously watched videos with a family member**: Sharing from history. *Not* public reposting.
- **g39 Play videos that produce white noise to help users fall asleep**: Sleep-aid content playback. *Not* medical insomnia treatment.
- **g40 Browse recommended content instead of searching for it**: Lean-back discovery via feed. *Not* targeted search.
- **g41 Access a variety of content types and view desired content**: Platform breadth (shorts, long, audio). *Not* creator tools.
- **g42 Customize content recommendations by specifying what to include and exclude**: User-driven tuning (topics, channels). *Not* fully manual curation.
- **g43 Discover new content beyond current recommendations**: Exploration/novelty beyond bubble. *Not* random content only.
- **g44 Receive viewing recommendations relevant to the user's stated interests**: Explicit preference signals. *Not* only implicit behavior.
- **g45 Understand how the internet works**: Learning objective for technical education content. *Not* app/network diagnostics.
- **g46 Limit the amount of personal information stored in a user account**: Privacy minimization (data retention/collection). *Not* anonymous usage necessarily.
- **g47 Provide a personalized content feed**: Higher-level “personalized feed exists.” *Not* specifying method.
- **g48 Allow users to immediately remove unwanted content types from their feed**: “Not interested” / topic removal controls. *Not* slow feedback loops.
- **g49 Help users transition from sleep or dreaming back to reality after waking up**: Gentle waking content/experience. *Not* alarm clock.

- **g55 Play a video in picture-in-picture mode**: PiP multitasking. *Not* split-screen necessarily.
- **g56 View a video in theater-style layout**: Intermediate layout. *Not* full screen.
- **g57 View a video in full-screen layout**: Full-screen viewing. *Not* VR.
- **g58 Open the short-form video page**: Enter shorts section. *Not* necessarily autoplay.
- **g59 Navigate away from the short-form video section**: Exit shorts, reduce doomscrolling. *Not* disabling shorts.
- **g60 Browse short-form videos by scrolling and loading more results**: Infinite scroll in shorts. *Not* paginated browsing.
- **g61 Search for short-form videos effectively**: Search UX for shorts. *Not* long-form search.
- **g62 Retrieve previously viewed videos later for sharing**: Find old videos specifically to share. *Not* general history browsing only.
- **g63 Skip advertisements**: Ad skipping capability (premium/controls). *Not* removing all monetization necessarily.
- **g64 Avoid sending long videos to others**: Discourage sharing very long items (social friction reduction). *Not* blocking sharing.
- **g65 Prevent extremely long advertisements from playing automatically**: Limit egregious ad length. *Not* remove ads entirely.
- **g66 Adjust playback speed**: Speed controls. *Not* pitch correction necessarily.
- **g67 Change video quality**: Resolution/bitrate selection. *Not* encoding settings.
- **g68 Filter search results by content duration**: General duration filtering. *Not* only >20 minutes.
- **g69 Filter search results by upload date range**: Freshness filtering. *Not* sorting only.
- **g70 Find the latest, in-depth information about a technical concept**: Use long-form + recency to learn. *Not* casual entertainment.
- **g71 Share short videos with friends and family to stay in touch**: Social connection via sharing shorts. *Not* in-app messaging necessarily.
- **g72 Make sharing videos easier**: Reduce steps to share. *Not* force sharing.
- **g73 Resolve issues when something is not working properly**: Troubleshooting support. *Not* developer debugging.
- **g74 Restore normal operation by reloading the page or restarting the session**: Basic recovery. *Not* deep fixes.
- **g75 Avoid switching platforms due to minor issues**: Retention goal via reliability. *Not* lock-in.
- **g76 Ignore unfamiliar new features**: Allow users to avoid unwanted changes. *Not* blocking all updates.
- **g77 Limit the amount of change introduced**: Change management. *Not* no innovation.
- **g78 Prevent changes from degrading the user experience**: Ensure updates don’t harm UX. *Not* guarantee zero regressions.

  Not intended: 100% accuracy guarantee.

### 1) What the software application is and does
The goals describe an **email and messaging application with an AI assistant layer**. It supports accessing email (via browser), reliably receiving mail, organizing and triaging an inbox, searching/filtering, summarizing and highlighting important content, and composing/sending emails (including scheduling, bulk send, groups/BCC, forwarding). It also includes productivity features around follow-up and deadlines, and collaboration features using shared categories. Overall, it helps users **manage high volumes of email/messages efficiently and safely**, with emphasis on job/school/work communications and assistant-supported reading/writing.

### 1) What the software application is and does
The goals describe an **email and messaging client with an AI assistant**. The application helps users **receive, organize, read, summarize, search, and respond to emails/messages**, with special emphasis on: reliability of delivery (including spam handling), productivity (triage, tagging, follow-ups, deadlines), assisted reading/writing (summaries, drafting), sending features (bulk, scheduled, recall/edit), accessibility/formatting, and message categorization/notification management. It also supports using email for work, recruiting/job applications, school updates, appointments, social communication, and professional networking.

### 2) Meaning of each goal in context (what is / is not intended)

- **g0 Help someone gain a deeper understanding of how users want to use a product**  
  *Means:* research/insight goal for product designers (the system helps collect/understand user needs).  
  *Not intended:* an end-user email feature; it’s a meta/analysis objective.

- **g1 Receive information about sales or discounts on merchandise**  
  *Means:* users receive promotional emails.  
  *Not intended:* the app itself selling merchandise; it’s about receiving such content.

- **g2 Analyze how users want to use email tools**  
  *Means:* product/UX analysis of user behavior and needs.  
  *Not intended:* directly an inbox feature; supports g0.

- **g3 Open a web browser to access email**  
  *Means:* use webmail via browser.  
  *Not intended:* building a browser; just supporting web access path.

- **g4 Use an assistant to read emails**  
  *Means:* AI reads/helps interpret emails (summaries, highlighting, etc.).  
  *Not intended:* replacing the user’s control; it augments reading.

- **g5 Use an assistant to write emails**  
  *Means:* AI drafting/support for composing emails.  
  *Not intended:* fully autonomous sending without review (unless user chooses).

- **g6 Use an email client primarily for work**  
  *Means:* work-focused usage context (priorities, volume, follow-ups).  
  *Not intended:* excludes personal use; just indicates primary scenario.

- **g7 Receive updates from recruiters about job applications**  
  *Means:* job-search related inbound messages are received and noticed.  
  *Not intended:* job application platform; it’s about communication.

- **g8 Check messages daily to avoid missing job-application-related updates**  
  *Means:* routine/behavior supported by notifications/triage.  
  *Not intended:* forcing daily checks; rather enabling not missing updates.

- **g9 Receive school news and notifications**  
  *Means:* inbound school announcements arrive and are managed.  
  *Not intended:* school management system; only consumption/organization.

- **g10 Book appointments with a dentist or clinic**  
  *Means:* scheduling via email/messages (requests, confirmations).  
  *Not intended:* full appointment booking engine; email-based coordination.

- **g11 Communicate with friends**  
  *Means:* personal messaging/email communication.  
  *Not intended:* social network features beyond communication.

- **g12 Network with professional contacts outside one’s organization**  
  *Means:* external professional communication, relationship maintenance.  
  *Not intended:* CRM platform; but may require organization/search.

- **g13 Review all received emails**  
  *Means:* inbox triage/processing so nothing important is ignored.  
  *Not intended:* reading every email in full; can be summarized/scanned.

- **g14 Receive emails in the inbox reliably**  
  *Means:* delivery, syncing, minimal loss.  
  *Not intended:* guarantee against sender-side failures; focus on client reliability.

- **g15 Receive periodic summaries of received emails**  
  *Means:* digest view (daily/weekly) of inbound messages.  
  *Not intended:* replaces real-time access; complements it.

- **g16 Use separate email accounts and categorize messages by purpose to organize emails**  
  *Means:* multi-account + purposeful categorization for organization.  
  *Not intended:* mandatory multiple accounts; supports optional strategy.

- **g17 Quickly scan emails to assess importance and reduce time spent reading**  
  *Means:* triage support (previews, highlights, summaries).  
  *Not intended:* deep comprehension; just importance assessment.

- **g18 Mark important emails**  
  *Means:* flag/star/priority marking.  
  *Not intended:* auto-marking only; could be manual or assisted.

- **g19 Read important emails**  
  *Means:* open and read prioritized messages.  
  *Not intended:* reading everything; focuses on importance.

- **g20 Generate a two- to three-sentence summary stating an email's purpose**  
  *Means:* AI summarization per email.  
  *Not intended:* long summaries or extracting every detail.

- **g21 Get assistance reading emails**  
  *Means:* broader reading support (summaries, highlighting, font).  
  *Not intended:* specifically voice-only; includes multiple assist methods.

- **g22 Delete spam or unwanted emails**  
  *Means:* remove spam/unwanted content.  
  *Not intended:* training a spam model necessarily; can be rules/filters.

- **g23 Delete unimportant emails to keep the inbox manageable**  
  *Means:* cleanup to reduce clutter.  
  *Not intended:* deleting important items; depends on importance assessment.

- **g24 Delete email conversations once they have concluded**  
  *Means:* lifecycle management/archival/deletion after completion.  
  *Not intended:* deleting for compliance; user-driven cleanup.

- **g25 Ensure important emails are not incorrectly placed in the spam folder**  
  *Means:* false-positive prevention; spam review/whitelisting.  
  *Not intended:* eliminating spam folder entirely.

- **g26 Tag emails or messages that require follow-up later**  
  *Means:* flagging tasks/reminders.  
  *Not intended:* full task manager; but integrates task cues.

- **g27 Search emails or messages**  
  *Means:* retrieval by keyword/sender/date/etc.  
  *Not intended:* enterprise eDiscovery; basic/advanced search for user.

- **g28 Filter emails or messages by tags**  
  *Means:* view subsets by tags/labels.  
  *Not intended:* only tags; could also filter by other facets.

- **g29 Return later to complete follow-up tasks associated with messages**  
  *Means:* reminder/queue to revisit tagged items.  
  *Not intended:* executing tasks inside email client; mainly tracking.

- **g30 Work on tasks by their deadlines**  
  *Means:* time management aided by follow-up/tagging/notifications.  
  *Not intended:* project management suite; supports deadline awareness.

- **g31 Send bulk messages to many recipients within a short time span**  
  *Means:* mass mailing capability.  
  *Not intended:* marketing automation platform; just bulk sending.

- **g32 Schedule messages to be sent at specified times**  
  *Means:* delayed send / send later.  
  *Not intended:* complex campaign scheduling; basic scheduling.

- **g33 Identify the main points and purpose of an email before drafting a response**  
  *Means:* comprehension aid prior to reply.  
  *Not intended:* writing the reply yet; preparatory step.

- **g34 Generate a well-organized email draft from provided main points, purpose, or a rough prompt.**  
  *Means:* AI-assisted drafting.  
  *Not intended:* final send without review.

- **g35 Edit an email draft before sending**  
  *Means:* user can revise before send.  
  *Not intended:* post-send editing (that’s g37/g38).

- **g36 Cancel sending an email shortly after sending it**  
  *Means:* undo send within window.  
  *Not intended:* guaranteed recall after delivery/read; limited window.

- **g37 Edit an email after it has been sent**  
  *Means:* post-send edit capability.  
  *Not intended:* standard SMTP email universally supports this; implies platform support.

- **g38 Allow recipients to view the current and previous versions of an email, including its edit history**  
  *Means:* versioning/audit trail for edited messages.  
  *Not intended:* hidden edits; transparency is intended.

- **g39 Warn the sender before sending an email when an attachment is mentioned but not included**  
  *Means:* attachment reminder.  
  *Not intended:* attach automatically (warning is minimal).

- **g40 Adjust font size**  
  *Means:* accessibility/readability control.  
  *Not intended:* full document styling suite.

- **g41 Automatically detect important sentences in an email and format them in bold.**  
  *Means:* AI highlighting of key lines.  
  *Not intended:* changing the sender’s original message permanently; likely a viewing format.

- **g42 Send emails**  
  *Means:* outbound email capability.  
  *Not intended:* covers messaging apps (that’s g43).

- **g43 Send messages**  
  *Means:* outbound messages in a messaging modality (could be chat/internal).  
  *Not intended:* necessarily SMS/WhatsApp; generic “messages”.

- **g44 Forward emails**  
  *Means:* send received email onward.  
  *Not intended:* auto-forward rules necessarily; could be manual.

- **g45 Send an email to a group of recipients**  
  *Means:* multi-recipient email.  
  *Not intended:* mailing list management beyond grouping.

- **g46 Send an email to a group of recipients using blind carbon copy**  
  *Means:* BCC group sending.  
  *Not intended:* anonymity guarantees beyond BCC semantics.

- **g47 Upload multimedia files to cloud storage**  
  *Means:* store large files externally.  
  *Not intended:* full DAM system; just upload/store.

- **g48 Send links to multimedia files instead of attaching the files directly**  
  *Means:* share via link to cloud storage.  
  *Not intended:* link-based access control complexities; basic sharing.

- **g49 Identify and highlight important messages and critical instructions or disclaimers within messages**  
  *Means:* AI detection of critical content within messages.  
  *Not intended:* legal compliance review; just highlighting.

- **g50 Provide notifications for important messages**  
  *Means:* alerting on priority messages.  
  *Not intended:* notifying on everything; prioritization is key.

- **g51 Summarize multiple messages into fewer messages while preserving key information**  
  *Means:* thread/digest summarization.  
  *Not intended:* losing nuance; preserve key info.

- **g52 Highlight important keywords in messages to prevent missing them**  
  *Means:* keyword highlighting for scanning.  
  *Not intended:* full NLP extraction; just highlight.

- **g53 Create and manage categories for messages and notifications**  
  *Means:* user-defined categories/labels for organization and notification tuning.  
  *Not intended:* fixed categories only; implies CRUD management.

- **g54 Automatically identify a category for each message or notification**  
  *Means:* auto-classification.  
  *Not intended:* perfect classification; likely user-correctable.

- **g55 Communicate with others using shared message categories**  
  *Means:* shared taxonomy/labels for group coordination.  
  *Not intended:* public tagging system; likely within a team/org.

### 1) What the software application is and does
This code describes a goal model for an **email and messaging client enhanced with an “assistant”** (AI-like features) that helps users **read, triage, summarize, organize, and compose emails/messages**, with added capabilities for **bulk/group sending, scheduling, attachment handling, versioning/undo-send, categorization/tagging, search/filtering**, and **important-message highlighting/notifications**. It is used primarily for **work and professional communication**, but also supports **personal communication** (friends), **school notifications**, **recruiting/job application updates**, **appointments**, and **marketing emails**.

---

### 2) What each goal means in context (including what is / is not intended)

- **g0 Help someone gain a deeper understanding of how users want to use a product**  
  *Means:* The meta-goal: use these goals to understand user needs for the email/messaging product.  
  *Not intended:* A runtime system feature; it’s a stakeholder/product discovery objective.

- **g1 Receive information about sales or discounts on merchandise**  
  *Means:* The inbox contains marketing/promotional emails the user wants to receive.  
  *Not intended:* The app generating discounts; only receiving/handling such emails.

- **g2 Analyze how users want to use email tools**  
  *Means:* Another meta/user-research goal feeding product design.  
  *Not intended:* End-user functionality.

- **g3 Open a web browser to access email**  
  *Means:* Users access email via webmail; the product must work in a browser.  
  *Not intended:* Building a browser; just supporting browser-based access.

- **g4 Use an assistant to read emails**  
  *Means:* AI assistance for reading: summaries, highlights, key point extraction, etc.  
  *Not intended:* Fully autonomous decision-making without user control.

- **g5 Use an assistant to write emails**  
  *Means:* AI assistance for drafting and refining outgoing emails.  
  *Not intended:* Sending messages without user review/intent.

- **g6 Use an email client primarily for work**  
  *Means:* Work-centric workflows (deadlines, follow-ups, professional comms) are primary.  
  *Not intended:* Excluding personal use; just prioritizing work features.

- **g7 Receive updates from recruiters about job applications**  
  *Means:* Reliable receipt and surfacing of recruiting-related emails.  
  *Not intended:* Managing applications; only communication handling.

- **g8 Check messages daily to avoid missing job-application-related updates**  
  *Means:* User behavior supported by notifications/summaries/important-marking.  
  *Not intended:* Forcing daily checking; the app supports but doesn’t mandate.

- **g9 Receive school news and notifications**  
  *Means:* Handling school-related notifications; categorization/priority helps.  
  *Not intended:* Being a school portal.

- **g10 Book appointments with a dentist or clinic**  
  *Means:* Email is used to coordinate scheduling; the app supports message handling and follow-ups.  
  *Not intended:* A booking system; just communication that enables booking.

- **g11 Communicate with friends**  
  *Means:* Personal messaging/email use.  
  *Not intended:* Social network features beyond messaging.

- **g12 Network with professional contacts outside one’s organization**  
  *Means:* External professional communication; supports organization, follow-up, drafting.  
  *Not intended:* CRM platform; only email/message capabilities.

- **g13 Review all received emails**  
  *Means:* A workflow objective: user can efficiently process inbox contents.  
  *Not intended:* Reading every email fully; could be scan/summarize.

- **g14 Receive emails in the inbox reliably**  
  *Means:* Delivery and inbox availability (sync, uptime, correct routing).  
  *Not intended:* Guarantee against all external email failures; focuses on system reliability.

- **g15 Receive periodic summaries of received emails**  
  *Means:* Digest view (daily/weekly) to help users keep up.  
  *Not intended:* Replacing inbox; it supplements.

- **g16 Use separate email accounts and categorize messages by purpose to organize emails**  
  *Means:* Multi-account support and organization by purpose (work/personal/school).  
  *Not intended:* Creating new email providers; just supporting multiple accounts and organization.

- **g17 Quickly scan emails to assess importance and reduce time spent reading**  
  *Means:* Triage support: previews, highlights, summaries, keyword emphasis.  
  *Not intended:* Automatically deleting/acting without confirmation.

- **g18 Mark important emails**  
  *Means:* Flagging/star/priority marking for later action.  
  *Not intended:* Only automated marking; can be user-driven too.

- **g19 Read important emails**  
  *Means:* Focused reading of priority items, aided by summaries/highlights.  
  *Not intended:* Ignoring non-important emails; just prioritization.

- **g20 Generate a two- to three-sentence summary stating an email's purpose**  
  *Means:* Short synopsis per email for quick understanding.  
  *Not intended:* Full detailed summarization; explicitly short purpose statement.

- **g21 Get assistance reading emails**  
  *Means:* General reading support umbrella (summaries, highlights, formatting).  
  *Not intended:* Writing/sending assistance (that’s g5).

- **g22 Delete spam or unwanted emails**  
  *Means:* Removing spam/unwanted messages; likely includes spam detection integration.  
  *Not intended:* Spam filtering alone; deletion is the action here.

- **g23 Delete unimportant emails to keep the inbox manageable**  
  *Means:* Reduce clutter by deleting low-value messages.  
  *Not intended:* Deleting items the user might need; implies safe triage.

- **g24 Delete email conversations once they have concluded**  
  *Means:* Lifecycle management: once a thread is done, remove/archive/delete.  
  *Not intended:* Deleting legal/required records automatically.

- **g25 Ensure important emails are not incorrectly placed in the spam folder**

  *Not intended:* Turning off spam protection entirely.

- **g26 Tag emails or messages that require follow-up later**  
  *Means:* Mark items needing action; integrate with workflow.  
  *Not intended:* Full task management suite; tags at least.

- **g27 Search emails or messages**  
  *Means:* Find content quickly via query.  
  *Not intended:* Enterprise eDiscovery; basic user search.

- **g28 Filter emails or messages by tags**  
  *Means:* View subsets based on applied tags/categories.  
  *Not intended:* Complex analytics; just filtering.

- **g29 Return later to complete follow-up tasks associated with messages**  
  *Means:* Deferred work supported by tags, reminders, saved views.  
  *Not intended:* Automatic completion of tasks.

- **g30 Work on tasks by their deadlines**  
  *Means:* Time management supported through reminders/priority/notifications.  
  *Not intended:* A full project management tool; minimal deadline support.

- **g31 Send bulk messages to many recipients within a short time span**  
  *Means:* Efficient broadcast emailing/messaging.  
  *Not intended:* Uncontrolled spam; assumes legitimate use.

- **g32 Schedule messages to be sent at specified times**  
  *Means:* Send-later functionality.  
  *Not intended:* Calendar scheduling beyond messaging.

- **g33 Identify the main points and purpose of an email before drafting a response**  
  *Means:* Assistant helps comprehension to respond appropriately.  
  *Not intended:* Drafting itself (that’s g34).

- **g34 Generate a well-organized email draft from provided main points, purpose, or a rough prompt.**  
  *Means:* AI drafting capability.  
  *Not intended:* Auto-send; user review still needed.

- **g35 Edit an email draft before sending**  
  *Means:* Manual editing tools and draft review workflow.  
  *Not intended:* Only AI edits; user edits implied.

- **g36 Cancel sending an email shortly after sending it**  
  *Means:* Undo-send within a window.  
  *Not intended:* Guaranteed recall after delivery/read.

- **g37 Edit an email after it has been sent**  
  *Means:* Post-send edit (typically link-based/live document style).  
  *Not intended:* Traditional SMTP guarantee; implies system-controlled message representation.

- **g38 Allow recipients to view the current and previous versions of an email, including its edit history**  
  *Means:* Version tracking/audit for post-send edits.  
  *Not intended:* Mandatory transparency for all emails; but that’s the feature intent.

- **g39 Warn the sender before sending an email when an attachment is mentioned but not included**  
  *Means:* Attachment detection and pre-send warning.  
  *Not intended:* Malware scanning or file management beyond warning.

- **g40 Adjust font size**  
  *Means:* Accessibility/readability UI control.  
  *Not intended:* Full document design suite.

- **g41 Automatically detect important sentences in an email and format them in bold.**  
  *Means:* Emphasis formatting for scanning.  
  *Not intended:* Changing original sender’s email permanently; could be viewer-side formatting.

- **g42 Send emails**  
  *Means:* Core capability to send email.  
  *Not intended:* Messaging apps (covered by g43).

- **g43 Send messages**  
  *Means:* Generic messaging (could include chat-like messages).  
  *Not intended:* Only email; broader than email.

- **g44 Forward emails**  
  *Means:* Re-send an email to another recipient.  
  *Not intended:* Sharing outside policy controls; no governance specified.

- **g45 Send an email to a group of recipients**  
  *Means:* Multi-recipient addressing (To/Cc).  
  *Not intended:* Mailing list management.

- **g46 Send an email to a group of recipients using blind carbon copy**  
  *Means:* BCC group send to protect recipient privacy.  
  *Not intended:* Hidden tracking or deception; just BCC capability.

- **g47 Upload multimedia files to cloud storage**  
  *Means:* Offload attachments to cloud.  
  *Not intended:* General cloud drive product; scoped to sending support.

- **g48 Send links to multimedia files instead of attaching the files directly**  
  *Means:* Replace attachment with share link.  
  *Not intended:* Permanent public links; access control unspecified.

- **g49 Identify and highlight important messages and critical instructions or disclaimers within messages**  
  *Means:* Assistant surfaces critical content.  
  *Not intended:* Legal compliance engine; just highlighting.

- **g50 Provide notifications for important messages**  
  *Means:* Alerts when priority items arrive.  
  *Not intended:* Notification for every message; importance-based.

- **g51 Summarize multiple messages into fewer messages while preserving key information**  
  *Means:* Thread/inbox summarization to reduce reading load.  
  *Not intended:* Removing details permanently; summary is a view.

- **g52 Highlight important keywords in messages to prevent missing them**  
  *Means:* Visual emphasis on key terms.  
  *Not intended:* Keyword-based censorship; just highlighting.

- **g53 Create and manage categories for messages and notifications**  
  *Means:* User-defined categories and management tools.  
  *Not intended:* Only automatic categorization (that’s g54).

- **g54 Automatically identify a category for each message or notification**  
  *Means:* Auto-classification.  
  *Not intended:* Perfect accuracy; implies user override.

- **g55 Communicate with others using shared message categories**  
  *Means:* Shared taxonomy/labels in collaboration contexts.  
  *Not intended:* Externally enforcing categories on recipients’ systems; could be internal/shared workspace.

- **g0 Help someone gain a deeper understanding of how users want to use a product**  
  *Means:* a meta/analysis goal: using the system (or research output from it) to understand user needs/behaviors around email.

  *Means:* user receives promotional emails.  
  *Not:* the system must market products; it just handles such emails.

- **g2 Analyze how users want to use email tools**  
  *Means:* research/analytics about user workflows in email.  
  *Not:* “analyze email content”; it’s about *users’ usage patterns*.

  *Means:* access email via web UI.  
  *Not:* requiring only web; just one access mode.

  *Means:* AI-supported reading (summaries, highlighting, read-aloud, etc.).  
  *Not:* full automation that removes user control.

- **g5 Use an assistant to write emails**  
  *Means:* AI drafting and improvement support.  
  *Not:* sending messages without user review.

- **g6 Use an email client primarily for work**  
  *Means:* work-centric workflow (priorities, follow-up, deadlines).  
  *Not:* excluding personal use.

- **g7 Receive updates from recruiters about job applications**  
  *Means:* important inbound messages from recruiters.  
  *Not:* a recruiting platform; it’s email handling.

- **g8 Check messages daily to avoid missing job-application-related updates**  
  *Means:* habit supported by the system via notifications/triage.  
  *Not:* forcing daily behavior—supporting it.

- **g9 Receive school news and notifications**  
  *Means:* inbound informational/alert messages from school.  
  *Not:* school portal replacement.

- **g10 Book appointments with a dentist or clinic**  
  *Means:* email used to coordinate scheduling (requests, confirmations).

  *Means:* relationship maintenance and outreach via email.  
  *Not:* CRM; though it may overlap in organization features.

  *Means:* inbox processing/triage to ensure nothing is missed.  
  *Not:* reading every word; can be via summaries/scan.

- **g14 Receive emails in the inbox reliably**  
  *Means:* deliverability and correct inbox placement.  
  *Not:* guaranteeing other senders’ systems; focuses on client-side handling and spam logic.

- **g15 Receive periodic summaries of received emails**  
  *Means:* digest view (daily/weekly) summarizing inbound messages.  
  *Not:* replacing the inbox; it’s a supplement.

- **g16 Use separate email accounts and categorize messages by purpose to organize emails**  
  *Means:* organization across accounts + categorization.  
  *Not:* forcing multiple accounts; optional strategy.

  *Means:* fast triage via snippets, highlights, AI.  
  *Not:* skipping critical details; only reducing effort.

  *Not:* automatic-only; can be user-driven.

  *Not:* reading *all* emails.

- **g23 Delete unimportant emails to keep the inbox manageable**  
  *Means:* inbox hygiene for low-value items.

  *Means:* cleanup after a thread is done.  
  *Not:* archival/recordkeeping requirement.

- **g25 Ensure important emails are not incorrectly placed in the spam folder**

  *Not:* eliminating spam filtering.

- **g26 Tag emails or messages that require follow-up later**

- **g43 Send messages**

- **g55 Communicate with others using shared message categories**

### 1) What the software application is and does (based on the goals)
This is an **email/messaging client with an AI assistant** aimed at helping users **receive, triage, read, organize, and respond to email efficiently**. It supports typical email actions (view inbox, search/filter, send/forward, group sending, scheduling) and adds assistant-powered capabilities (summaries, highlighting important content, drafting replies). It also emphasizes **reliability and inbox hygiene** (spam control, deleting unimportant/concluded threads) and **task follow-up/workflow** (tagging, returning later, meeting deadlines). The app is used for mixed purposes: work email, recruiters/job updates, school notifications, friends/social, professional networking, shopping/discounts, and appointment booking.

- **g0 Help someone gain a deeper understanding of how users want to use a product**  
  *Means:* support user research/insight (likely for product teams) by analyzing how people use email tools.  
  *Not intended:* it’s not a user-facing inbox feature by itself; it’s an outcome about understanding needs.

- **g1 Receive information about sales or discounts on merchandise**  
  *Means:* user gets promotional emails successfully delivered and visible.  
  *Not intended:* not necessarily recommending purchases or managing coupons.

- **g2 Analyze how users want to use email tools**  
  *Means:* gather/analyze usage patterns, needs, pain points regarding email tooling.  
  *Not intended:* not “analyze emails content for marketing” per se; it’s about user behavior/needs.

- **g3 Open a web browser to access email**  
  *Means:* access email via webmail flow.  
  *Not intended:* not implying the product is only browser-based; just one access method.

- **g4 Use an assistant to read emails**  
  *Means:* AI reads/summarizes/highlights content for the user.  
  *Not intended:* not necessarily full automation without user control.

- **g5 Use an assistant to write emails**  
  *Means:* AI helps draft responses/messages.  
  *Not intended:* not necessarily auto-sending without review.

- **g6 Use an email client primarily for work**  
  *Means:* work-focused usage; prioritization for work communications.

The application is a **digital reading and course-content management system** optimized for **tablet-based reading**. It lets users (especially students) **access public web content and official news**, **collect and consolidate course PDFs/eBooks and web articles into a personal online library**, **store that library across cloud providers and e-reader accounts**, and **support a less cumbersome, more focused reading experience** with progress/time-remaining indicators. It also supports a **school workflow** where instructors can assign articles to students in a single place.

### Goal-by-goal meaning (in this application context)

- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**: The overall desire to consume reading materials in digital form. Not specifically about how (tablet vs computer) or where content comes from.
- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**: Optimize UX for tablets; implies mobility/touch reading. Not about eliminating desktop support entirely.
- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**: Reduce friction (too many steps, format switching, repeated downloading/uploading). Not about the content itself being “easy.”
- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**: Help readers stay engaged (e.g., fewer context switches, unified interface, progress indicators). Not explicitly about blocking distractions or implementing website blockers.
- **g4 Access and read public web content online**: Ability to read normal web pages in-app or via a dedicated reading flow. Not necessarily about paywalled or private LMS content.
- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**: A school-oriented workflow (assignment distribution, student access, persistence across semester). Not a full LMS replacement.
- **g6 Read news online from official sources**: Support following news sites directly (including trials). Not about social media or user-generated news.
- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**: A “library” concept holding PDFs/eBooks/articles metadata. Not necessarily full document editing.
- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**: Integration with multiple clouds (e.g., Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive) and possibly e-reader accounts. Not implying the app becomes the storage provider.
- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**: Retention and retrieval over time; not limited to currently enrolled courses.
- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**: Manage/enable trial-based access flows. Not endorsing bypassing paywalls illegally; intended to use legitimate trial mechanisms.
- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**: Direct export/ingestion flows from web/LMS to cloud/library. Not forbidding downloads; it’s about not requiring them.
- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**: Ability to fetch PDFs from portals/pages when needed. Not about uploading PDFs created locally.
- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**: Unified reader for multiple formats. Not necessarily advanced annotation or editing.
- **g14 Manage PDF documents**: Organize, rename, delete, move, tag, maybe basic metadata. Not full PDF authoring.
- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**: Interoperability (share/open-in). Not implying one-way only; just capability to hand off.
- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**: Tablet compatibility for document opening. Not specifically about offline access (though could be).
- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**: Reduce steps in getting materials onto the tablet (sync, export to cloud, direct open). Not necessarily about speed/performance.
- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**: Save to user-owned storage (cloud drive / local files). Not necessarily inside the app only.
- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**: The act of downloading for ownership/offline use. Not a replacement for direct-export flows.
- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**: “Zero-desktop” workflow; teachers/students can send directly to storage. Not excluding optional desktop use.
- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**: Concrete export target category. Not limited to one provider.
- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**: Send to Kindle/other e-reader services. Not necessarily bi-directional sync.
- **g23 Consolidate all reading materials into a single location**: A single hub/library view regardless of source/provider. Not necessarily physically copying content; could be aggregation/indexing.
- **g24 View the percentage of completion for the current chapter**: Reading progress UI. Not about grading or course completion.
- **g25 View the estimated time remaining to finish the current chapter**: Time-to-finish indicator. Not guaranteeing accuracy.
- **g26 Save valuable documents and resources for later access**: Bookmark/save-for-later across web/articles/docs. Not necessarily long-term archival guarantees.
- **g27 Categorize resources by time period and enable filtering or searching by month or year, including for saved resources based on when they were read**: Time-based organization and retrieval. Not necessarily full-text search of document contents.

The application is a digital reading workflow tool aimed at students (and more generally readers) that centralizes online articles, news, PDFs, and eBooks into a personal online library and makes them easy to access and read—especially on a tablet. It focuses on reducing friction in getting content from the web/course portals into a single reading interface, enabling storage across cloud providers, supporting exporting/sharing to other readers (cloud storage and e-reader accounts), and providing reading-progress aids to help maintain focus.

### Goal-by-goal meaning (in this application context)

- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**: The overall outcome is that users consume reading materials in digital form within the tool’s ecosystem. Not intended: digitizing paper books via scanning/ OCR.
- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**: Prioritizes tablet-optimized access/UX. Not intended: replacing all computer-based workflows (e.g., heavy editing) beyond reading-centric tasks.
- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**: Minimize friction like too many steps, format fragmentation, slow loading, and context switching. Not intended: solving all web usability issues outside the app’s control (e.g., broken publisher sites).
- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**: Provide features that support uninterrupted reading and awareness of progress. Not intended: clinical attention support or blocking all distractions system-wide.
- **g4 Access and read public web content online**: Ability to read publicly available web pages/articles in-app. Not intended: bypassing paywalls or accessing private/institution-restricted content without permission.
- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**: Tailor workflows for classes (assigned readings, course materials, tablet use). Not intended: full LMS replacement (grading, quizzes, etc.).
- **g6 Read news online from official sources**: Ensure users can consume news from publishers’ official sites/feeds. Not intended: guaranteeing accuracy/bias detection.
- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**: Central library concept inside the app (even if backed by providers). Not intended: public sharing repository by default.
- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**: Integrate multiple backends (e.g., Google Drive, OneDrive). Not intended: building a new storage provider.
- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**: Persistence/retention and continued access. Not intended: overriding institutional access revocation (e.g., if a portal removes files).
- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**: Support lawful trial-based access flows and manage the reading experience during trials. Not intended: subscription circumvention.
- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**: Streamline “send to library/reader” without manual local file shuffling. Not intended: never caching locally (the app may cache for performance).
- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**: Acquire PDFs from course sources into the workflow. Not intended: hacking into restricted portals.
- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**: Unified reader UI for common formats. Not intended: full authoring/editing suite.
- **g14 Manage PDF documents**: Organize, rename, tag, delete, move, etc. Not intended: advanced PDF editing like redaction/desktop publishing.
- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**: Share/send PDFs out to other apps. Not intended: ensuring the other reader supports all features/annotations.
- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**: Tablet compatibility for document viewing. Not intended: support for every tablet OS/version indefinitely.
- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**: Reduce steps from discovery to availability on tablet. Not intended: eliminating all authentication steps required by schools/providers.
- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**: Save acquired files to the user’s chosen storage. Not intended: mandatory cloud-only storage (could be optional).
- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**: Provide downloading capability to user storage. Not intended: enabling piracy; assumes authorized downloads.
- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**: “Direct-to-cloud” transfer from source to storage. Not intended: bypassing security restrictions.
- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**: Generic export target: Drive/Dropbox/etc. Not intended: only one provider.
- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**: Send to Kindle/other e-reader services. Not intended: guarantee of delivery if provider rejects file/format.

### 1) What the software application is and does
The goals describe a **digital reading application optimized for tablets** (especially in a school setting) that helps users **access, collect, store, and read online and document-based materials** (web articles, news, PDFs, eBooks). It reduces friction in getting content onto a tablet, provides a **single reading interface**, supports **cloud/library storage across providers**, and adds **reading progress/focus features**. It also supports an instructor workflow for assigning articles, and a student workflow for collecting materials and presenting proposals.

### 2) What each goal means (and what it does *not* mean)

- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**  
  *Means:* The overall outcome: reading happens in digital form (web, PDFs, eBooks).  
  *Not intended:* Creating content, publishing, or buying books.

- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**  
  *Means:* Tablet is the primary reading device; flows should be tablet-friendly.  
  *Not intended:* Excluding computers entirely (could still support them), but prioritizes tablet.

- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**  
  *Means:* Reduce steps, avoid messy conversions, minimize context switching, simplify exporting/importing.  
  *Not intended:* General performance tuning unrelated to reading workflows.

- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**  
  *Means:* Support features that keep attention on the reading task (progress/time remaining, consolidated materials, single interface).  
  *Not intended:* Clinical attention tracking, surveillance, or classroom monitoring.

- **g4 Access and read public web content online**  
  *Means:* Read normal web pages/articles directly online.  
  *Not intended:* Paywalled/private content access hacks.

- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**  
  *Means:* A workflow and experience suited for courses: assignments, course materials, later retrieval.  
  *Not intended:* Full LMS replacement (grading, quizzes, rosters), unless explicitly added.

- **g6 Read news online from official sources**  
  *Means:* Consume news directly from publishers/official sites (and potentially via trials).  
  *Not intended:* Social media news feeds or unofficial aggregators as primary sources.

- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**  
  *Means:* Persistent library of reading materials tied to the user.  
  *Not intended:* Public sharing repository or institutional archive.

- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**  
  *Means:* Integrations to keep content in different clouds (Drive/Dropbox/etc.).  
  *Not intended:* Building a new storage provider; it’s orchestration/integration.

- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**  
  *Means:* The library persists beyond a course lifecycle.  
  *Not intended:* Guaranteeing instructor/course portal access after the course ends; instead, preserve copies in the user’s library/storage.

- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**  
  *Means:* Legitimate use of trials/promotions; manage access windows.  
  *Not intended:* Circumventing paywalls illegally.

- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**  
  *Means:* Streamlined “send to library/tablet/cloud” workflows without manual file shuffling.  
  *Not intended:* No offline support; offline might still require downloads.

- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**  
  *Means:* Capture PDFs from course sites and web pages into the system.  
  *Not intended:* Scraping protected systems without authorization.

- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**  
  *Means:* One reader UI for PDFs and eBooks (consistent experience).  
  *Not intended:* Full editing/authoring for those formats.

- **g14 Manage PDF documents**  
  *Means:* Organize PDFs (rename, move, tag, delete, maybe annotate).  
  *Not intended:* Full PDF authoring suite.

- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**  
  *Means:* Ability to hand off PDFs to other apps/services.  
  *Not intended:* Lock-in; it explicitly supports portability.

- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**  
  *Means:* Tablet compatibility for opening/reading docs.  
  *Not intended:* Desktop-only features.

- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**  
  *Means:* Reduce friction from “found on web/LMS” to “readable on tablet”.  
  *Not intended:* Eliminating all user choice; may still require confirmation.

- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**  
  *Means:* Save acquired files into the user’s chosen cloud/file storage.  
  *Not intended:* Only internal app storage; this implies external/personal storage.

- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**  
  *Means:* Save materials locally in the user’s storage space (often cloud).  
  *Not intended:* Only temporary caching.

- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**  
  *Means:* Instructor/student can push assigned materials to cloud storage directly.  
  *Not intended:* Requires computer as intermediary; explicitly avoids it.

- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**  
  *Means:* Generic export to Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive/etc.  
  *Not intended:* Only one provider.

- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**  
  *Means:* Send to Kindle/other e-reader ecosystems.  
  *Not intended:* Replace those ecosystems.

- **g23 Consolidate all reading materials into a single location**  
  *Means:* One hub/library that indexes content even if stored across providers.  
  *Not intended:* Physically storing everything in one backend only; could be federated.

- **g24 View the percentage of completion for the current chapter**  
  *Means:* Reading progress indicator to support focus/planning.  
  *Not intended:* Grades or instructor analytics.

- **g25 View the estimated time remaining to finish the current chapter**  
  *Means:* Time estimate to support planning and sustained focus.  
  *Not intended:* Productivity surveillance.

- **g26 Save valuable documents and resources for later access**  
  *Means:* Bookmark/save-to-library behavior (including web resources).  
  *Not intended:* Long-term citation management, though it overlaps.

- **g27 Categorize resources by time period and enable filtering or searching by month or year, including for saved resources based on when they were read**  
  *Means:* Timeline-based organization and retrieval (read date, saved date).  
  *Not intended:* Full semantic search across text content (not stated).

- **g28 Access assigned school articles in a single online location on a tablet**  
  *Means:* A tablet-friendly “assigned readings” area.  
  *Not intended:* Full course management.

- **g29 Receive assigned articles from instructors**  
  *Means:* Instructor-to-student distribution mechanism.  
  *Not intended:* Messaging/chat generally (unless needed for assignments).

- **g30 Present a project proposal to an instructor**  
  *Means:* Student submits proposal (likely related to reading/research).  
  *Not intended:* Full project management lifecycle.

### 1) What the software application is and does (from the goals)
The application is a **tablet-centered digital reading and document workflow tool** aimed largely at **students in a school setting**, but also useful for personal reading (news and public web content). It helps users **access online reading materials (web pages, PDFs, eBooks, news)**, **store and consolidate them into a personal online library across providers**, **move materials to tablets/e-readers with fewer steps**, and **support focused reading** with progress/time indicators. It also supports an instructor-driven workflow for **assigning articles to students**, and includes a small academic workflow element around **presenting a project proposal to an instructor**.

### 2) Meaning of each goal in context (what is / is not intended)

- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**  
  *Means:* Overall desire to consume reading materials in digital form rather than print.  
  *Not intended:* Does not specify device, storage, or workflow.

- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**  
  *Means:* Preference for tablet-first reading experience.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily excluding phones/e-readers; focus is “not on a computer”.

- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**  
  *Means:* Reduce friction: fewer steps, less switching apps, less downloading/uploading.  
  *Not intended:* Not primarily about content quality or cost.

- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**  
  *Means:* Features that help concentration (single interface, progress indicators).  
  *Not intended:* Not medical/clinical attention support; not blocking all distractions necessarily.

- **g4 Access and read public web content online**  
  *Means:* Read open web pages/articles directly online.  
  *Not intended:* Not about paywalled content unless via trials/subscriptions.

- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**  
  *Means:* A school-appropriate workflow: assignments, consistent access, tablet usage.  
  *Not intended:* Not a full LMS replacement; scoped to reading.

- **g6 Read news online from official sources**  
  *Means:* Access reputable/official publisher sources rather than reposts.  
  *Not intended:* Not about social media/news aggregation from unofficial channels.

- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**  
  *Means:* Central personal repository/index of reading materials.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily institutional storage or shared library for all students.

- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**  
  *Means:* Connect multiple clouds/accounts and store/sync materials.  
  *Not intended:* Not building a new storage provider; it orchestrates existing ones.

- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**  
  *Means:* Retain access post-course (not removed when class ends).  
  *Not intended:* Not guaranteeing access if provider deletes content; implies retention support.

- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**  
  *Means:* Take advantage of legitimate trial windows to read paywalled news.  
  *Not intended:* Not piracy/bypassing paywalls; stays within official trial mechanisms.

- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**  
  *Means:* Direct export/save-to-cloud/e-reader without manual file shuffling.  
  *Not intended:* Not forbidding downloads entirely; just reducing need.

- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**  
  *Means:* Acquire PDFs from course sites/portals.  
  *Not intended:* Not about authoring PDFs.

- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**  
  *Means:* Unified reader UI for common formats.  
  *Not intended:* Not full-featured editing; primarily reading.

- **g14 Manage PDF documents**  
  *Means:* Organize/rename/tag/move PDFs, perhaps annotate lightly.  
  *Not intended:* Not full PDF editing suite unless implied by “manage”.

- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**  
  *Means:* Ability to hand off PDFs to other apps (interop).  
  *Not intended:* Not locking users into the app.

- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**  
  *Means:* Tablet compatibility for document viewing/reading.  
  *Not intended:* Not requiring tablet-only; but must work well on tablets.

- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**  
  *Means:* Streamlined import pipeline from web/portal/cloud to tablet.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily automatic; just fewer manual steps.

- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**  
  *Means:* Save files into user-controlled storage location (cloud drive, etc.).  
  *Not intended:* Not only storing inside the app sandbox.

- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**  
  *Means:* Support downloading and saving locally/cloud into user storage.  
  *Not intended:* Not always required; alternative is direct export.

- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**  
  *Means:* For instructor-assigned items, one-click save to cloud.  
  *Not intended:* Not limited to PDFs only, though often is.

- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**  
  *Means:* Generic “save to Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive/etc.”  
  *Not intended:* Not specifying providers.

- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**  
  *Means:* Send-to-Kindle / e-reader service integration.  
  *Not intended:* Not building its own e-reader ecosystem.

- **g23 Consolidate all reading materials into a single location**  
  *Means:* Unified library/index even if stored across providers.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily physically moving all files; could be logical consolidation.

- **g24 View the percentage of completion for the current chapter**  
  *Means:* Progress indicator per chapter to support pacing/focus.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily for all formats unless chapters exist.

- **g25 View the estimated time remaining to finish the current chapter**  
  *Means:* Time-to-complete estimate to support pacing/focus.  
  *Not intended:* Not guaranteed accuracy; uses reading speed heuristics.

- **g26 Save valuable documents and resources for later access**  
  *Means:* Bookmark/save items into library for future retrieval.  
  *Not intended:* Not implying sharing; personal saving.

- **g27 Categorize resources by time period and enable filtering or searching by month or year, including for saved resources based on when they were read**  
  *Means:* Organization and retrieval via time-based metadata and search/filter.  
  *Not intended:* Not full semantic search; specifically time period facets.

- **g28 Access assigned school articles in a single online location on a tablet**  
  *Means:* Student view: one tablet-friendly place for assigned readings.  
  *Not intended:* Not necessarily the only place assignments exist (LMS may still exist).

- **g29 Receive assigned articles from instructors**  
  *Means:* Instructors can push/assign; students can receive.  
  *Not intended:* Not grading/assessment; just delivery/assignment.

- **g30 Present a project proposal to an instructor**  
  *Means:* A student can submit/present a proposal (likely document-based).  
  *Not intended:* Not a full project management suite; this is a discrete workflow.

The application is a digital reading and content-management tool aimed at students (and generally anyone reading online) that: (a) supports reading web articles, PDFs, and eBooks on a tablet in a single interface; (b) reduces friction in getting course materials from the web/course portals into a personal library and onto a tablet; (c) organizes and retains materials across semesters; (d) tracks reading progress to help maintain focus; and (e) supports exporting/archiving content to external storage providers and e-reader accounts.

## Goal-by-goal meaning (in this application)
- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**: The overall intent is to consume reading materials in digital form within the system’s ecosystem. Not intended: printing, physical book logistics, or authoring content.
- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**: Optimize the experience for tablet use (touch UI, portability). Not intended: forbidding computer use; it’s a preference/primary target device.
- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**: Reduce steps, context switching, clunky workflows, and poor readability. Not intended: “offline-only” reading or replacing every website UI.
- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**: Provide features that reduce distraction and help the reader stay oriented. Not intended: enforcing discipline; it supports focus rather than guaranteeing it.
- **g4 Access and read public web content online**: Open/read freely available web articles in-app (or via integrated view). Not intended: bypassing paywalls or accessing private/intranet content without permission.
- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**: Support instructor-assigned readings, student access, and school workflows. Not intended: full LMS replacement (grading, attendance, etc.).
- **g6 Read news online from official sources**: Enable reading news content from publishers/sources. Not intended: aggregating pirated copies; “official” implies legitimate access paths.
- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**: Maintain a personal, persistent library of materials. Not intended: a public shared library for everyone by default.
- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**: Integrations with multiple cloud/file providers. Not intended: building a new storage provider; it coordinates existing ones.
- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**: Long-term retention and retrieval. Not intended: institutional archival guarantees; it’s user-centric access.
- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**: Support legitimate free trials/promotions for reading. Not intended: subscription circumvention beyond allowed trial terms.
- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**: Avoid manual “download then re-upload” steps; enable direct import/export/streaming. Not intended: never caching; some downloads may still occur automatically.
- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**: Provide capture/import of PDFs from typical course sources. Not intended: hacking access to restricted portals.
- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**: Unified reader experience across formats. Not intended: advanced editing/authoring; it’s primarily for reading.
- **g14 Manage PDF documents**: Organize, rename, tag, delete, move, perhaps annotate (ambiguous). Not intended: full Acrobat-level editing unless specified later.
- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**: Ability to hand off PDFs to external apps. Not intended: forcing export; it’s optional interoperability.
- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**: Ensure tablet compatibility and workflows. Not intended: exclusive tablet support; but tablet is key.
- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**: Streamlined ingestion to tablet. Not intended: eliminating all steps; rather minimizing manual operations.
- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**: Save captured files into the user’s chosen storage (cloud drive, etc.). Not intended: only local device storage.
- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**: Enable downloads into user storage. Not intended: downloading content that the user cannot legitimately access.
- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**: Direct-to-cloud export. Not intended: bypassing permissions; assumes the user has access.
- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**: Generic export integration. Not intended: only one provider; it’s a broad capability.
- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**: Send content to Kindle/other accounts. Not intended: DRM-breaking conversions.
- **g23 Consolidate all reading materials into a single location**: A unified “hub” view/library across sources/providers. Not intended: physically moving all files; may be logical consolidation.
- **g24 View the percentage of completion for the current chapter**: Progress tracking per chapter/section. Not intended: perfect accuracy for all PDFs without structure.
- **g25 View the estimated time remaining to finish the current chapter**: Time-to-finish estimates based on reading speed/length. Not intended: guaranteed precision.
- **g26 Save valuable documents and resources for later access**: Bookmark/save for later retrieval. Not intended: permanent guarantee without storage backing.
- **g27 Categorize resources by time period and enable filtering or searching by month or year, including for saved resources based on when they were read**: Time-based organization and retrieval. Not intended: full bibliographic cataloging; it’s time-centric filtering/search.
- **g28 Access assigned school articles in a single online location on a tablet**: Student-facing view of assigned readings on tablet, unified. Not intended: necessarily offline access.
- **g29 Receive assigned articles from instructors**: Instructor-to-student distribution/assignment mechanism. Not intended: students sourcing everything themselves.
- **g30 Present a project proposal to an instructor**: A school workflow beyond reading—submitting/presenting proposals. Not intended: full project management; it’s a specific submission/presentation step.

### 1) What the software application is and does
The goals describe a **tablet-first digital reading application** used by students (and potentially general readers) to **access, collect, store, and read online and document-based materials** (web pages, PDFs, eBooks, news), with an emphasis on **school workflows** (assigned readings, course portals, instructor distribution) and **reducing friction** (fewer steps, no download/re-upload), while also supporting **reading progress and focus** and **personal library management across cloud providers**.

### 2) Goal-by-goal meaning (including intent / non-intent)

- **g0 Read books and articles digitally**  
  *Intent:* Overall outcome: the user consumes reading content in digital form.  
  *Not intended:* Any particular device, file type, or workflow.

- **g1 Read on a tablet instead of a computer**  
  *Intent:* Preference/constraint: primary reading occurs on a tablet device.  
  *Not intended:* Excluding phones/e-readers entirely, but emphasizes tablet as the target.

- **g2 Avoid a cumbersome online reading experience**  
  *Intent:* Minimize friction (too many steps, context switching, awkward formats).  
  *Not intended:* Doesn’t define exact usability metrics; it’s a quality goal.

- **g3 Maintain focus while reading**  
  *Intent:* Support concentration (single interface, progress cues, fewer interruptions).  
  *Not intended:* Medical/clinical attention tools; no claim of improving cognition.

- **g4 Access and read public web content online**  
  *Intent:* Read publicly available web pages without needing specialized portals.  
  *Not intended:* Bypassing paywalls/DRM; only “public” content.

- **g5 Provide a dedicated method for online reading in a school setting**  
  *Intent:* A school-oriented workflow for distributing and consuming readings.  
  *Not intended:* Full LMS replacement (grading, quizzes) unless later added.

- **g6 Read news online from official sources**  
  *Intent:* Access news content directly from publishers/official outlets.  
  *Not intended:* Aggregating pirated copies; may still involve subscriptions/trials.

- **g7 Store books and course materials in a personal online library.**  
  *Intent:* Persist a curated library for later retrieval.  
  *Not intended:* Institution-owned repository; it’s “personal”.

- **g8 Store library content across multiple storage providers.**  
  *Intent:* Integrate multiple clouds (e.g., Drive, Dropbox) as backing storage.  
  *Not intended:* Building a new storage provider; more like connectors.

- **g9 Access previously stored course materials after a course or semester ends.**  
  *Intent:* Long-term retention and retrieval for materials already saved.  
  *Not intended:* Access to materials the user never stored or no longer has rights to.

- **g10 Use free-trial access to read news content without paying for an ongoing subscription**  
  *Intent:* Support trial-based reading flows where legitimately available.  
  *Not intended:* Circumventing subscription rules or repeated “trial abuse”.

- **g11 Access reading materials without needing to download and upload them**  
  *Intent:* Streamlined acquisition/transfer (direct export, cloud-to-app).  
  *Not intended:* Eliminating caching/offline entirely; just avoiding manual steps.

- **g12 Download course-related PDF documents from web pages and course portals**  
  *Intent:* Acquire PDFs from typical academic sources for reading/storage.  
  *Not intended:* Scraping restricted portals without permission.

- **g13 Open and read PDF and eBook documents in a single interface**  
  *Intent:* Unified reader UI for multiple document types.  
  *Not intended:* Full authoring/editing suite.

- **g14 Manage PDF documents**  
  *Intent:* Organize/rename/move/annotate/mark-up (scope not fully specified).  
  *Not intended:* Advanced desktop-class PDF production unless specified.

- **g15 Export PDF documents to another document reader**  
  *Intent:* Interoperability—hand off to other apps when needed.  
  *Not intended:* Forced export; it’s optional.

- **g16 Open documents, including PDF files, on a tablet**  
  *Intent:* Tablet compatibility for document reading.  
  *Not intended:* Necessarily offline-only; just device support.

- **g17 Import course content to a tablet with fewer steps**  
  *Intent:* Reduce steps from source (portal/web) to tablet library/reader.  
  *Not intended:* Removing all authentication steps; just reducing unnecessary friction.

- **g18 Store downloaded documents in personal file storage.**  
  *Intent:* Save files into user-controlled storage (likely cloud drive).  
  *Not intended:* Only local device storage; “personal file storage” implies cloud or user account.

- **g19 Download reading materials to personal file storage.**  
  *Intent:* Capture content into the user’s storage for persistence/offline.  
  *Not intended:* Only PDFs; could include other formats depending on implementation.

- **g20 Export assigned reading materials directly to online storage without downloading them to a computer first.**  
  *Intent:* Direct-to-cloud export, avoiding computer intermediary.  
  *Not intended:* Eliminating all downloads everywhere; it’s about avoiding the computer step.

- **g21 Export content to a cloud storage location.**  
  *Intent:* General capability to save/export to cloud.  
  *Not intended:* Only one provider (ties to g8).

- **g22 Export content to an e-reader account.**  
  *Intent:* Send documents to services like Kindle, etc.  
  *Not intended:* Guaranteeing perfect formatting for every e-reader.

- **g23 Consolidate all reading materials into a single location**  
  *Intent:* One “hub” experience even if storage is distributed.  
  *Not intended:* Physically moving all files to one provider; could be logical aggregation.

- **g24 View the percentage of completion for the current chapter**  
  *Intent:* Reading progress indicator (chapter-level).  
  *Not intended:* Necessarily accurate for arbitrary PDFs without structure.

- **g25 View the estimated time remaining to finish the current chapter**  
  *Intent:* Time-to-complete estimate to support planning/focus.  
  *Not intended:* Guaranteed accuracy; it’s an estimate.

- **g26 Save valuable documents and resources for later access**  
  *Intent:* Bookmark/save items (web pages, documents) for later retrieval.  
  *Not intended:* Full bibliographic reference manager unless specified.

- **g27 Categorize resources by time period and enable filtering or searching by month or year, including for saved resources based on when they were read**  
  *Intent:* Time-based organization and retrieval (read date / saved date).  
  *Not intended:* Only time-based categorization; could coexist with tags/courses.

- **g28 Access assigned school articles in a single online location on a tablet**  
  *Intent:* Tablet-based “assigned reading” feed/library in one place.  
  *Not intended:* Public web browsing generally; it’s specifically assigned articles.

- **g29 Receive assigned articles from instructors**  
  *Intent:* Instructors can distribute links/files/reading lists to students.  
  *Not intended:* Students discovering content themselves; that’s separate.

- **g30 Present a project proposal to an instructor**  
  *Intent:* A student submits/presents a proposal through the system (or supported workflow).  
  *Not intended:* Full project management; may be lightweight submission/presentation.
